subject: efficient generation of a distribution of Bayesian p-values

messages.author: 7fe97f8ba9e0dcfe
messages.subject: efficient generation of a distribution of Bayesian p-values
parts:
Hello!

I am trying to set up simulation code to generate a distribution of Bayesian p-values. The idea is for each of n simulated datasets, I will fit the model and calculate a Bayesian p-value using the observed data and posterior predictive replicated data.

I am trying to avoid compiling the model over and over again for each simulated dataset, so I am hoping to repeatedly use the same compiled model. Also as a note, I am adding simulated data to the model, rather than simulating data with the model, since I am trying to develop a workflow where the model can be the wrong data-generating process.

With the below code, in the second iteration of the n_datasets loop, I am getting the following error in the compileNimble(mcmc, project = compiled_model) part of the fit_model() function. 
Error in nimbleProject$instantiateCmodelValues(thisObj, dll) : Trying to instantiate a modelValues type that the project has no record of. Try setting option resetFunctions = TRUE in compileNimble

It seems like the MCMC settings need to be reset somehow? And also, I'm wondering if there are any general tips on setting this up to be the most efficient?

Thanks so much!
Abby Keller 

The general code set-up is like this:

# create model instance and compile
model <- nimbleModel(model_code, constants = constants)
compiled_model <- compileNimble(model)

for (i in 1:n_datasets) {
 
  # add simulated data to compiled model 
  compiled_model$y <- simulate_data(params)
 
  # fit model
  samples <- fit_model(model, compiled_model, niter, nburnin, thin)
 
  # calculate p values
  p_values[i, "deviance"] <- mean(samples[, "D_rep_total"] > samples[, "D_obs_total"])
  p_values[i, "chi_sq"] <- mean(samples[, "chi_rep_total"] > samples[, "chi_obs_total"])
}

Where fit_model() looks like this:

fit_model <- function(model, compiled_model, niter, nburnin, thin) {
 
  # function for generating initial values
  inits <- function(y) list(psi = runif(1, 0, 1), p = runif(1, 0, 1), z = pmin(rowSums(y), 1))
 
  # add initial values
  compiled_model$setInits(inits(compiled_model$y))
 
  # configure MCMC
  mcmc_conf <- configureMCMC(model,
                             monitors = c("psi", "p", "z", "D_obs_total", "D_rep_total", 
                                                      "chi_obs_total", "chi_rep_total"))
 
  # build and compile MCMC
  mcmc <- buildMCMC(mcmc_conf)
  compiled_mcmc <- compileNimble(mcmc, project = compiled_model)
 
  # generate posterior samples
  samples <- runMCMC(compiled_mcmc, niter = niter, nburnin = nburnin, thin = thin)
 
  return(samples)
}

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: efficient generation of a distribution of Bayesian p-values
parts:
hi Abby,

I think this is a case where you should be able to reuse a single compiled MCMC and not need to keep rebuilding and compiling the MCMC.

In the later datasets (after all the usual steps for the first dataset) I think you should be able to put the new `y` values into the compiled model (as you are doing), and then rerun the MCMC using the existing compiled MCMC via `runMCMC`. You will probably want to reset the initial values in the compiled model at the start of each MCMC such that they are not the last values from the previous MCMC (it looks like you already have code to do this, though I don't know if `psi`, `p`, and `z` are the only parameters being sampled). Then it should work. So you shouldn't need the `configureMCMC`, `buildMCMC`, or `compileNimble` steps except for when `i=1`.

Let us know if that doesn't work.

As a sidenote, if you were not able to reuse the compiled MCMC, this might be a situation in which using the `resetFunctions` argument to `compileNimble` might be relevant, but I think that is moot, given my suggestion above.

-chris
